sites_playshelf: Your game library, on the console
privacy_1: This site sets no cookie, and keeps nothing in your browser but the language you choose in its header. It loads nothing from another site: its fonts, images and scripts are served with it.
privacy_2: It counts its visits with Umami Cloud, in the European Union (Frankfurt), without cookie. For each page seen: the page, the page you came from, your browser, system and kind of device, your screen's size, your language and your country. Your IP address is used to tell your country and to tell visits apart, and is not kept with them. The counts are kept six months, used only to know what is read, and never sold or shared. Umami's policy: umami.is/privacy.

title_home: Lantern · An open protocol for game library servers
description_home: Lantern is an open, versioned protocol between the game library servers people run at home for their own games and the homebrews and apps that read them, on every platform Aurore runs on. Draft 0.4.
description_spec: The Lantern protocol, draft 0.4: platforms and their profiles, discovery, pairing, the library, downloads checked by SHA-256, game data, homebrew and game ports, save backups, cheats, errors and limits.
footer_made: A Boréale project. The specification's text under CC BY 4.0, everything else under MIT.
hero_title: From your server to your console, one open protocol.
hero_lede: Lantern is an open, versioned contract between the library servers people run at home for their own games and the homebrews and apps that read them, on a console, a phone, a computer or in the browser: browse the library, download with integrity checks, install homebrew, keep save backups and cheats.
status_text: The text may still change before 1.0. Comments are welcome, from client and server authors especially.
solid_title: What it covers, and what makes it solid
solid_lede: Draft 0.4 binds each token to its device, adds invitations, an administration API and rating caps, and gives every requirement an id that the conformance suite names. Draft 0.3 brought every platform Aurore runs on, homebrew and game ports, game data, saves and cheats. Underneath, Lantern starts fresh: it is compatible with no earlier protocol, so every choice serves safety and the long run.
covers_platforms: Every platform Aurore runs on: Nintendo Switch, New 3DS, PS Vita, PS4, Android, iOS and tvOS, Windows, macOS, Linux and the browser. A core that knows no platform, and a profile for each.
covers_homebrew: Homebrew, game ports included: a manifest gives each file its place, nothing is written elsewhere without your consent, and an author's signature is checked when there is one. A port runs on the data of your own copy of the game, which Lantern never serves.
covers_titles: Game data: genres, players, age ratings, a summary and images in your language, read a hundred at a time.
covers_saves: Save backups, sent in chunks that survive a lost connection, and checked when they arrive.
covers_cheats: Cheats: several sets for each version of a game, in each platform's own format.
solid_versions: Versioned twice, in the path and in every document: a change never breaks a client in silence.
solid_tokens: A token per device, approved on the server and revocable one by one: no password is ever typed on the console or kept there.
solid_https: HTTPS everywhere. A server at home with its own certificate is pinned when the console pairs, once you have compared its key's fingerprint on both screens.
solid_content: Verified content: every file comes with its SHA-256, which the console checks before installing anything.
solid_features: Declared features: the server says what it offers, to whom, and in which schema.
solid_suite: A conformance suite that checks a server from outside, and a reference server that passes it.
solid_pages: Cursor pages that neither skip nor repeat while the library changes.
solid_errors: Errors with real status codes, all in one format.
solid_nothing: Nothing hidden: no hardware identifier, no proprietary encryption, no change to the client decided by the server.
implement_lede: The specification is short: few routes, fixed shapes, plain HTTP and JSON.
server_text: Serve the handshake and the library, and pairing when your server is private; add game data, homebrew, save backups or cheats when you want, and declare them in its features. A server fits in a weekend.
client_text: Find servers on the local network, name your platform, read their features, page through the library and check each download's SHA-256. A client fits in a few hundred lines of C++.
schemas_text: A JSON Schema for every document, an example of each, and an OpenAPI description of the routes, to check your own against.
implement_soon: In the repository: a conformance suite to run against a server (conformance/), which prints the levels it reaches, and a small reference server that passes it (server/). Only an implementation that passes the suite at a level may call itself “Lantern compatible” and show the badge of that level.
first_client: The first client will be PlayShelf, a homebrew package manager for the Nintendo Switch.
own_text: Lantern carries what your server holds, between it and your console. It finds nothing and distributes nothing: it is not a way to get games, and its servers are for the games you own.
licence_text: The specification's text: share and adapt it, naming where it comes from.
licence_rest: Everything else (schemas, OpenAPI description, examples, conformance suite, reference server), so that any server or client, under any licence, can implement the protocol and copy its schemas as they are.
licence_compatible: Questions, comments and proposals go to the repository's issues.

closing_text: The draft is the time to change things. An issue about a route, a field or a missing case helps every server and client to come.
spec_lede: REST and JSON, versioned by path and by a schema in every document. Sixteen short sections, and an annex for the platforms.
spec_english: The specification is written in English only, and the English text is the reference.
sites_atlas: A map of every game, on every platform
sites_lantern: The protocol between servers and consoles
covers_keys: Tokens bound to the device: a key made at pairing signs every request, so a token copied off a console works nowhere else. Pairing by QR code, with the code and the key's fingerprint still beside it.
covers_admin: Invitations for a few devices and a few days, a small administration API to approve a console from your phone, and a rating cap carried by a token: what is rated above it disappears, on the server's side.
covers_quality: An id for every requirement, a threat model, conformance levels and the “Lantern compatible” badge, test vectors for libraries, and guidelines for clients.
covers_more: Errors and the server's message in your language, compressed JSON, Atlas ids, installed sizes, and withdrawing your own request.
conformance_title: Levels, a badge, and who passes
conformance_text: The suite prints the levels a server reaches, from Lantern Core to +admin. Every requirement of the text has an id, and the traceability page says which check of the suite covers it, and which ones only a client can keep.
